claim: Chunked KV-cache compression introduces a positional coordinate — a token's phase, its position modulo the compression stride S — and retrieval accuracy in models using it varies sharply and periodically with that phase.
stance_target: the repo's claim that CSA-style compressed attention has a training-time failure mode that average benchmarks do not show
scope_conditions: Chunked KV-cache compression (CSA family) in DeepSeek-V4 and in from-scratch Qwen3-0.6B-backbone pretrains; NIAH retrieval at 128K and 2K
quoted_support: We uncover a systematic asymmetry in models using such compression: the same information can be easy to retrieve at one phase and difficult at another. We call this periodic variation in retrieval performance phase sensitivity.

claim: At 128K context, retrieval accuracy in the DeepSeek-V4 family differs by up to 40 percentage points across phases; the measured best-worst residue gaps are 40.23pp (V4-Flash-Base), 19.14pp (V4-Flash-0731), 34.77pp (V4-Pro-Base), 14.84pp (V4-Pro-0813) and 6.09pp (V4.1-Flash).
stance_target: the claim that CSA-family compression trades average long-context accuracy for systematic positional weak spots
scope_conditions: Single-token needle-in-a-haystack at 128K context, 2,048 prompts per model (2,560 for V4.1-Flash), eight residue groups mod 8 spanning two stride-4 cycles
quoted_support: At 128K context, retrieval accuracy in the DeepSeek-V4 family can differ by up to 40 percentage points across phases. ... Their best-worst residue gaps are 40.23, 19.14, 34.77, and 14.84 percentage points, respectively. ... DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, evaluated on 2,560 prompts per residue group, has a mean accuracy of 92.38% and a best-worst residue gap of 6.09 percentage points.

claim: DeepSeek-V4's compressed sparse attention uses a compression stride of S = 4, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base's top-1 completion of its own inference code flips with exactly that four-token period as only filler length is varied.
stance_target: the repo's description of CSA as a stride-4 chunked compression
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base completing inference/kernel.py; 16 filler lengths L=24..39; code content held fixed
quoted_support: In particular, the model predicts 8 ... tokens, matching the stride S = 4 of DeepSeek-V4's compressed sparse attention (CSA).

claim: The effect reproduces in from-scratch pretraining at 0.6B scale: a family of Qwen3-0.6B-backbone transformers trained for 100B tokens (sequence length 2,048, global batch 1,024 sequences, BF16, AdamW, 47,518 steps) with KV compression as the only architectural change all show phase sensitivity with period equal to their stride.
stance_target: the feasibility of testing CSA-style compression inside this box's compute budget (0.6B params, 100B tokens, 2k context)
scope_conditions: Qwen3-0.6B architecture backbone; reference W8/S8; strides 4/6/8/12; uniform-average gates; no-RoPE and partial-RoPE variants; DeepSeek-V4 CSA kernel ported to the Qwen backbone
quoted_support: We pretrain from scratch a broad family of transformers with the Qwen3-0.6B architecture [27] as backbone and KV compression as the only substantial architectural modification ... The reference 100B-token training run uses AdamW with (beta1, beta2) = (0.9, 0.95), epsilon = 1e-8, weight decay 0.1, and gradient clipping at norm 1. Training uses BF16 and seed 42. The packed corpus is traversed once with sequence length 2,048 and a global batch of 1,024 sequences.

claim: Every compressed variant is phase-sensitive while full-attention baselines are flat: Prefix-Padding accuracy gaps reach up to 78 percentage points for compressed models against at most 6.1 percentage points for full-attention baselines.
stance_target: the claim that the periodicity is caused by chunked compression rather than by the backbone or the task
scope_conditions: Qwen3-backbone pretrains, NIAH with 64 key-value pairs, Prefix Padding protocol, W8/S8 reference and variants
quoted_support: Every compressed model we evaluate shows periodicity matching the compression stride, including models that simply average token representations within each window. By contrast, full-attention baselines have no comparable periodicity. ... The same holds for every compressed run in Table 8, with Prefix Padding gaps of up to 78 percentage points against at most 6.1 for the baselines.

claim: Average accuracy conceals the failure: the 8-KV-head W8/S8 compressed model nearly matches its full-attention baseline on mean accuracy and validation loss, yet its worst phase reaches only 9.9% accuracy against 58.4% for the baseline.
stance_target: the repo's claim that CSA2's payoff cannot be judged on average loss or average benchmark scores
scope_conditions: Qwen3-backbone W8/S8 model with 8 KV heads vs full-attention baseline at comparable validation loss
quoted_support: With eight KV heads, the W8/S8 compressed model nearly matches its full-attention baseline in mean accuracy and validation loss, yet its worst residue is only 9.9%, against 58.4% for the baseline.

claim: The period follows the compression stride, not the window: at W=8, strides S in {4, 6, 8} give periods of about four, six and eight tokens, and W4/S4 shares W8/S4's four-token period despite a smaller window.
stance_target: the mechanism claim that phase = position mod stride is the right coordinate
scope_conditions: Qwen3-backbone pretrains; W in {4, 8, 12}, S in {4, 6, 8, 12}; overlapping and non-overlapping windows
quoted_support: Varying window and stride separately shows that the period follows the stride in the tested geometries, whether or not windows overlap. At W = 8, strides S in {4, 6, 8} give periods of about four, six, and eight tokens.

claim: Phase sensitivity is not an artifact of learned gates or rotary embeddings: it persists when uniform averaging replaces the gates and when RoPE is removed entirely.
stance_target: the claim that the failure is intrinsic to chunked compression, so a CSA2 training run should expect it regardless of positional-encoding choices
scope_conditions: Qwen3-backbone pretrains; uniform-gate variant (Figure 11), NoPE variant (Figure 3h), partial-RoPE (dr=16)
quoted_support: In these experiments, phase sensitivity needs neither rotary position embeddings (RoPE) nor learned gates: it persists without RoPE (Figure 3h) and when uniform averaging replaces the gates (Figure 11).

claim: The DeepSeek-V4 CSA kernel itself, ported onto the Qwen backbone, reproduces phase sensitivity — so the failure is a property of the CSA kernel, not of DeepSeek's training data or scale.
stance_target: whether a CSA2-style kernel can be evaluated cheaply on this box before committing to a full training run
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4 CSA kernel used on the Qwen3-0.6B backbone; Figure 3i
quoted_support: The family also includes DeepSeek-V4's CSA kernel [11], which tests whether the kernel studied in Section 2 produces phase sensitivity while being used on the Qwen backbone.

claim: Causal interventions (KV-head knockouts, attention-readout mean replacement) show phase specialization: different heads and layers contribute asymmetrically to retrieval at different source phases, and in DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base the odd layers using heavily compressed attention (HCA, compression rate 128) contribute little to retrieval.
stance_target: the claim that compressed layers do qualitatively different work from full-attention layers, which bears on how many Full-mode layers a CSA2 config needs
scope_conditions: Qwen3-backbone pretrains and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base; knockout of one layer's KV head per row, columns grouped by source position mod 8
quoted_support: In (c), the pattern also repeats with period four, matching the CSA stride, and the odd layers, which use heavily compressed attention (HCA) with compression rate 128, contribute little to retrieval.

claim: An idealized induction task proves that gradient flow drives compression gates toward sharp, persistent phase preferences even though future queries are unknown — the specialization is a training-dynamics outcome, not a data artifact.
stance_target: the claim that phase specialization emerges during pretraining, so it will appear in any CSA2 training run on this box
scope_conditions: Idealized induction task with compressed attention, linear compressors, population loss, Euclidean gradient flow from small random initialization
quoted_support: We show that the optimal compressor favors particular phases, and gradient flow drives gates toward persistent preferences.

claim: The authors' prescription is to evaluate compressed-attention models across phases — e.g. by shifting the input a few tokens while holding the queried information fixed — because high average accuracy can coexist with systematic positional failures.
stance_target: the evaluation protocol any CSA2 experiment on this box should adopt
scope_conditions: Any model using chunked KV-cache compression
quoted_support: Evaluating models with chunked KV-cache compression thus requires measuring across compression phases: high average accuracy can coexist with systematic positional failures.

claim: DeepSeek-V4 keeps exact tokens only in a local window, so the compressed branch is the only route to distant tokens — there is no exact fallback branch that could mask a compressed-branch failure (unlike hybrids such as NSA).
stance_target: the claim that CSA2's compression is load-bearing for long-range retrieval, not an optimization on top of exact attention
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V4 architecture; comparison to hybrid sparse-attention designs with an exact distant branch
quoted_support: DeepSeek-V4 keeps exact tokens only in its local window [11], and we find phase ... In hybrids that keep an exact branch over distant tokens, such as NSA [41], that branch could mask a failure of the compressed branch alone.
